title: Reconcile FP-MCP-217 With Popup-Approved Local Clearance
summary: Record an explicit governance reconciliation for the conflict between FP-MCP-217 and FP-MCP-232. FP-MCP-217 established that MCP may observe and validate operator-local clearance, but must not create it; the final clearance act belonged outside the model-callable MCP surface. FP-MCP-232 introduced forgepilot_create_operator_local_execution_clearance, a popup-approved MCP tool that creates the clearance artifact. This is not merely a UX improvement; it is a weaker and different safety posture that revises the FP-MCP-217 boundary if adopted. This packet does not ratify the popup-mediated posture merely because it worked once. It opens the policy decision explicitly and requires a follow-up decision before popup-mediated clearance is used for further real starts.
caveats: FP-MCP-232/233 are classified as functionally successful but governance-incomplete until this reconciliation is resolved.
A ChatGPT approval popup is still inside the model-callable MCP tool surface and does not satisfy the original FP-MCP-217 hands-on-keyboard outside-MCP boundary.
The fact that the FP-MCP-233 run succeeded must not be used to launder or retroactively justify the boundary change.

Both outcomes remain valid for the reconciliation: restore FP-MCP-217 original local-shell clearance requirement, or deliberately adopt popup-mediated clearance with documented threat-model changes and compensating controls.
Popup-mediated clearance should not be used for additional real starts until a follow-up decision explicitly resolves this reconciliation.
This checkpoint itself does not disable or remove the FP-MCP-232 tool; it records the governance state and required decision before further use.

previousPosture.rule: MCP may observe and validate operator-local clearance but should not create it; final execution clearance is a human-local hands-on-keyboard act outside the model-callable MCP surface.
previousPosture.securityProperty: model cannot manufacture the final local authorization artifact through an MCP call

newPostureIntroduced.ruleActuallyImplemented: MCP may create one exact, short-lived local clearance artifact after a ChatGPT/MCP approval popup and validation checks.
newPostureIntroduced.securityPropertyChanged: human approval becomes approval of a model-proposed tool invocation inside the MCP surface, not an independent outside-MCP shell action

threatModelDelta.oldRiskControl: model-callable MCP surface could not write execution-clearance.json at all
threatModelDelta.newRiskControl: model can propose a clearance-writing tool call, but human must approve the popup and the tool enforces exact tuple, expiry, clean workspace, approval validity, and no runner contact
threatModelDelta.residualRisk: user may approve a model-proposed clearance creation without independently initiating the action outside MCP; the model-callable surface now includes a clearance writer

decisionOptions: RESTORE_FP_MCP_217_ORIGINAL_BOUNDARY: retire or restrict forgepilot_create_operator_local_execution_clearance for real starts; require hands-on-keyboard local clearance outside MCP.
ADOPT_POPUP_MEDIATED_CLEARANCE: explicitly revise FP-MCP-217 and allow popup-approved MCP clearance creation only under strict exact-scope constraints.
HYBRID: allow popup-mediated clearance only for low-risk DESIGN_ONLY canaries or local/dev environments, while requiring outside-MCP clearance for higher-risk run modes.

requiredFollowUp.purpose: Decide whether popup-mediated local clearance is acceptable, restored, or restricted; record explicit policy result before any further real start uses the FP-MCP-232 tool.

relatedIntegrityIssues: FP-MCP-233 first real start lacked explicit evidence for full FP-027 canary discipline: process-tree snapshot immediately before contact, abort-readiness live and checked, and explicit no-retry/no-chaining state-machine evidence.
FP-MCP-233 approval was not mechanically consumed after start because of the FP-MCP-234 hardcoded scope bug, creating a bounded reuse window until expiry.
A separate integrity-review packet should record the FP-MCP-233 historical gaps without erasing the successful engineering result.
